subject: Medalia Health — EU-only hosting, SCCs, backups & retention Q&A

Subject: EU-only hosting + SCCs questions

Hi Jordan,

Thanks for the demo last week. As we discussed in procurement, Medalia needs strict EU-only processing for patient-identifiable prompts and model I/O. Before we move forward we need clarity on several items tied to Schrems II / SCCs:

- Confirm whether production inference, backups, and logs can be constrained to EU regions only.
- How are backups handled (retention, cross-region replication, deletion guarantees)?
- Who (if anyone) can access decrypted data for troubleshooting — can operator/engineering access be restricted or escrowed?
- Do you provide SCCs (EU Standard Contractual Clauses) and can Redwood accept addendum language about operator access and deletion SLAs?

Attached: Medalia’s retention matrix and a shortlist of contract asks. Could you please loop in privacy and legal?

Best,
Elena

Subject: Re: EU-only hosting + SCCs questions

Hi Elena — thanks, and great questions. Looping in our legal and privacy leads + infra to respond precisely. High-level answers up front:

- We can provision a EU-only processing environment (compute + primary storage) in the customer’s requested region(s).
- Backups are configurable: we offer in-region snapshots with an option to keep encrypted backups only in EU. Cross-region replication is opt-in and disabled by default for EU-only contracts.
- Operator access: by default we require limited engineer access for emergency troubleshooting; however we support contractual guardrails (role-based MFA, Just-In-Time access, recorded sessions) and can negotiate stricter operator access conditions for enterprise customers.
- SCCs: we provide the EU SCCs and are open to a limited addendum covering operator access and retention commitments — will hand to Lauren for legal language.

Naomi, Karthik, Lauren — can each confirm the specifics below (retention enforcement, backup deletion timeline, KMS ownership, runbook for operator access)?

Next: I propose a short M.A.P. (mutual action plan) for follow-up and a proposed redline on SCCs — happy to set a call with Medalia & our legal team.

Thanks,
Jordan
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Date: 2026-09-21T08:35:00Z
Subject: RE: EU-only hosting + SCCs questions

Hi Elena — Naomi from Privacy & Compliance here.

Short answers with the controls we can commit to in contract:

1) Scope: We will designate the Medalia production tenant and associated storage as EU-only. This scope includes inference compute, model artifacts, logs, and primary object storage used for customer prompt/response payloads.

2) Backups: We support two backup modes for EU customers: (A) In-region encrypted snapshots retained for configured retention window only; (B) In-region encrypted snapshots plus long-term archival (also EU-only). Cross-region replication is explicitly disabled unless Medalia directs otherwise. Backup deletion is irreversible; we will run a deletion job that removes snapshot metadata and wipes encryption keys per schedule.

3) Retention guarantees: We can contract to enforce maximum retention periods per data class (e.g., raw prompts 30 days, model-level cache entries 7 days) — see the attached retention matrix you supplied. We will provide an audit artifact showing deletion job completion times upon request.

4) Operator access & emergency access: By default support engineers may access operational logs and redacted traces. For Medalia we can offer a hardened model:
   - No human access to plaintext model I/O without a documented JIT access request and explicit Medalia approval.
   - All JIT access requests are logged, video-recorded, and time-limited.
   - Option to escrow an operator access affidavit with a named third-party auditor (region-limited).

5) SCCs & contract language: Redwood will sign EU SCCs. We can accept a short addendum addressing operator access constraints, backup residency, and deletion SLA (for example: backups removed within X hours after retention expiry; escrow procedures defined). Lauren will propose clause text.

I’ll also note limitations: complete elimination of human access in every failure mode is operationally challenging; the escrow + auditable JIT approach is our recommended compromise that many healthcare customers accept. Happy to walk through technical controls on a call.

Best,
Naomi Feldman
Privacy & Compliance — Redwood Inference

Subject: RE: EU-only hosting + SCCs questions — infra specifics

Hi all — Karthik from Infra. Technical points to confirm implementation options:

- KMS / Key ownership: We support two modes: (1) Redwood-managed keys (we hold the key material in an EU KMS managed by Redwood); (2) Customer-managed keys (Medalia supplies keys via Bring-Your-Own-Key (BYOK) in a partner KMS in the EU). For the highest assurance pick BYOK — Redwood will not be able to decrypt past the KMS gate and we can write contract obligations around key lifecycle.

- Backups & snapshots: Snapshots are encrypted at rest. For EU-only tenants we can disable snapshot export APIs. Physical deletion of snapshots involves secure wipe of underlying storage and deletion of snapshot metadata; complete eradication also requires key destruction (if keys are managed by Redwood we will retire the key material upon deletion per the agreed SLA).

- Logs & telemetry: Application-level logs can be configured to redact PII and retain only hashed identifiers. Operational metrics and host logs are stored with separate retention and can be excluded from cross-region logging pipelines.

- Failover & fallback: If a regional outage requires cross-region failover, we will only failover to another EU region by default. Cross-border failover to non-EU regions is subject to Medalia’s approval and will be treated as a contractual exception (with notice).

I can provide a short runbook for JIT access, key rotation, and deletion proof artifacts (sha256 manifests of deleted snapshot IDs) if helpful.

-Karthik

Subject: RE: EU-only hosting + SCCs questions — proposed contract language & MAP

Hi Elena and Oliver — Lauren from Legal. Thanks for the detailed tech notes. Attached is a short redline we propose to the SCCs that adds: (a) explicit operator access constraints (JIT, audit, third-party escrow option), (b) backup residency & deletion SLA (within 72 hours of retention expiry for Tier 1 data), and (c) BYOK responsibilities & key rotation obligations.

Key asks from Redwood’s side: we request reasonable exception windows for emergency troubleshooting and to retain ephemeral logs for debugging (time-limited), both subject to Medalia’s approval for each incident when the hardened operator mode is selected.

Next steps / Mutual Action Plan (MAP):
- Jordan to schedule a 45-min call with Medalia + Redwood legal/privacy/infra (by 2026-09-27).
- Medalia to review the attached redline and provide markups (by 2026-10-04).
- Redwood to provide runbook and JIT access template & sample audit record (Karthik/Naomi) (by 2026-09-28).
- Finalize SCCs addendum and BYOK operational checklist (target signature: 2026-10-15).

Oliver — please share any immediate redline feedback; we can include a DocuSign link once markups settle.

Thanks,
Lauren Bishop
Senior Counsel — Redwood Inference
